'''Anonym.OS''' was a [[live CD]] operating system based on [[OpenBSD]] 3.8 with strong [[encryption]] and anonymization tools. The goal of the project was to provide secure, anonymous [[internet|web browsing]] access to everyday users.<ref name=Wired>
{{cite web
 |url=https://www.wired.com/news/technology/internet/0,70017-0.html?tw=wn_tophead_1 
 |title=Anonyity on a Disc 
 |publisher=[[Wired.com]] 
 |date=January 14, 2006 
 |author=Quinn Norton 
 |accessdate=November 6, 2011 
 |url-status=dead 
 |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20070211022729/http://www.wired.com/news/technology/internet/0%2C70017-0.html?tw=wn_tophead_1 
 |archivedate=February 11, 2007 
}}
</ref> The operating system was [[OpenBSD]] 3.8, although many [[Software package (installation)|packages]] have been added to facilitate its goal. It used [[Fluxbox]] as its [[window manager]].

The project was discontinued after the release of Beta 4 (2006).

==Distributed==

Designed, created and distributed by [https://kaos.to kaos.theory/security.research].

==Legacy==

Although this specific project is no longer updated, its successors are Incognito OS (discontinued in 2008) and [[FreeSBIE]].<ref>
{{cite web
|url=http://distrowatch.com/table.php?distribution=anonymos
|title=Anonym.OS LiveCD
|publisher=[[DistroWatch]]
|accessdate=November 6, 2011}}</ref>
